best_for: Developers on Windows or Mac who want to see branches and commits as a graph and stage changes with clicks, often alongside Bitbucket or GitHub.

points.title: Free, but needs an Atlassian account
points.text: Sourcetree is a free download, yet setup asks you to accept Atlassian's customer agreement and sign in with an Atlassian account. Linking Bitbucket or GitHub is optional and can be skipped.

points.title: Git with the extras built in
points.text: It shows your history as a graph and supports Git LFS for large files and git-flow branching out of the box. The homepage also lists Mercurial support.

points.title: Two different apps
points.text: Windows and Mac are developed apart: Windows is on 3.4.33 and Mac on 4.2.21. Menus, features and fixes do not always match between them.

points.title: Update for 3.4.33's fixes
points.text: The Windows 3.4.33 release on 31 October 2026 closed several security holes, including remote code execution through repository settings and Git-flow branch names. Older Windows versions here carry those flaws.

points.title: No Linux build
points.text: Atlassian ships Sourcetree for Windows and Mac only. Linux users need another Git client.

points.title: Windows installers and versions
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 33 versions, with per-user installers for x86 and x64 that need no admin rights and a machine-wide MSI for x64. macOS lists only the current release, a universal zip.
